= GitHub Actions

This file describes how the workflows in `.github/workflows/` behave today.
A Claude mention is a maintainer's comment, review, or issue body that asks Claude to run.
A Claude issue PR is a pull request Claude opened for an issue, on a branch named `claude-issue-<number>-...`.
Each Codex review of a new commit counts as one round.
Every job runs on `ubuntu-latest`.
Jobs other than Continuous Integration that install dependencies use Node `26.x`.
Jobs that run Claude read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and commit through the GitHub API.

== Overview

`ci.yaml` runs on every pull request, and on a push to `main` or to a `vX.Y.x` branch.
Renovate opens one pull request per dependency, and `dependency-review.yaml` may add one follow-up commit.
Codex reviews Renovate pull requests and Claude issue PRs on its own.
`codex-review.yaml` handles those findings, and `codex-watchdog.yaml` flags a pull request Codex has not reviewed.
A Claude mention, or the `claude` label, runs `claude.yaml` on any issue or pull request except a release.
`publish-pr.yaml` opens the release pull request.
After the maintainer squash-merges it and pushes a signed tag, `publish.yaml` publishes the package.
The maintainer creates the GitHub Release by hand.

== ci.yaml

Continuous Integration runs on a push to `main`, on a push to a `vX.Y.x` branch, and on every pull request.
The job runs once for each of Node `22.x`, `24.x`, and `26.x`.
Each version runs `npm ci`, then `npm run lint:build`, then `npm run dist`.
There are no tests yet.

== dependency-review.yaml

Dependency Review runs when Renovate opens, reopens, or updates a pull request that Renovate authored.
Adding the `claude-review` label reruns it.
Claude follows the `update-dependency` skill and may push one signed follow-up commit.
When the job succeeds, it triggers `codex-review.yaml`.

== claude.yaml

`claude.yaml` runs when a maintainer writes a Claude mention or adds the `claude` label.
It skips a release issue and a pull request from a `publish-v` branch.
`publish-pr.yaml` handles those.
For an issue, this workflow opens a Claude issue PR.
A later mention on that pull request keeps working on the same branch.
Ask for follow-ups on the pull request: a run on the issue checks out `main` and cannot commit.
This workflow and `codex-review.yaml` share the lock `claude-<number>`, so only one of them pushes at a time.

== codex-review.yaml

`codex-review.yaml` runs when Codex posts or edits its summary on a Renovate pull request or a Claude issue PR.
It also runs after Dependency Review succeeds.
It ignores a pull request from a `publish-v` branch.
The maintainer reviews those.
Claude fixes open findings for two rounds.
After the third review, the workflow only reports the remaining findings.
A failed review, or a summary this workflow cannot read, adds the `help wanted` label.

== codex-watchdog.yaml

Codex Review Watchdog runs every hour, and a maintainer can run it by hand.
It checks open Renovate pull requests and Claude issue PRs.
When the latest commit is at least two hours old and has no Codex review, the job comments and adds `help wanted`.
It does this once per commit.

== publish-pr.yaml

`publish-pr.yaml` runs when a maintainer adds the `claude` label to an open release issue.
The issue title must be `Release @perfective/build vX.Y.Z`.
It also runs when a maintainer writes a Claude mention on the release pull request.
The job stops when that version's tag already exists, or when its pull request is already merged.
If `publish-vX.Y.Z` already exists, Claude continues on that branch.
Claude commits one change titled `Publish vX.Y.Z`.
That commit may include only the version, the lockfile, the changelog, the READMEs, and the roadmap.
This workflow does not create the tag, and it does not publish to npm.

== publish.yaml

`publish.yaml` runs when a tag matching `v*` is pushed.
The tag must be annotated, GitHub must verify its signature, and the commit must be on `main` or on `vX.Y.x`.
`package.json` must carry that version, and `CHANGELOG.adoc` must contain a section for it.
The job runs `lint:build` and `dist`, then publishes `./dist` with provenance.
It signs in to npm with GitHub's OIDC token.
The npm dist-tag is one of the following:

* `latest`, for a release on `main`
* `backport-X.Y`, for a release on a backport branch
* `next`, for a prerelease

This workflow does not create a GitHub Release.
Do not rename this file: npm trusted publishing is bound to the name `publish.yaml`.

== Renovate

`renovate.json` makes Renovate open one pull request per dependency, with no automerge.
`rangeStrategy` is `bump`, so the version pin in `package.json` moves together with the lockfile.
A major update, a peer dependency update, and a TypeScript update receive the `help wanted` label.
The label `renovate-regenerate` tells Renovate to recreate the branch.
